title: Man. Post. Cap. IX: truth needs no art; commentary confuses the status
pass_a_gloss: If conjecture is allowed, you meant thereby to occupy and fortify readers' minds lest they be wounded by the stings of Placeus's replies and reasons. If that was your counsel, you seem to him to have distrusted and hurt your own cause. For truth does not need such art; simple, open, ingenuous, candid, even when humble it breathes something noble, and trusting the God of truth most rejoices and shines when set beside its contrary, however painted. Whether by that counsel or another, what you did disturbs and scatters our dispute and forces much repetition.
pass_b_english: If room is to be given to conjecture, you wished by that means to occupy and fortify the minds of readers, lest they be wounded by the stings of my replies and reasons. In which, if this was your counsel, you seem to me to have distrusted and hurt your cause. For truth does not desire an art of this kind; simple, open, ingenuous, candid, even when it is humble, it breathes something noble, where (in which it is stronger than every thing) and trusting the God of truth it then most rejoices and shines and gleams, when it is compared with its contrary, however painted. But that, whether it was done by you with that counsel or another, disturbs our dispute, and scatters it, and forces much to be repeated.
source_text: Si conjecturae locus dandus est, ea ratione animos lectorum occupare voluisti ac praemunire, ne mearum responsionum & rationum aculeis laederentur. In quo, si hoc tuum consilium fuit, videris mihi causae tuae diffidisse ac obfuisse. Veritas enim artem hujusmodi non desiderat; simplex, aperta, ingenua, candida, humilis etiam cum sit, generosum quid spirat, ubi (qua omni re fortior est) & Deo veritatis fidens tum maxime laetatur & splendet & fulget, cum suo contrario, ut ut fucato, comparatur. Id autem, sive isto sive alio consilio a te sit factum, nostram disputationem conturbat, & distrahit, & multa cogit repetere.
